raw_response:
I will split my 20 mu into two parts. I will keep 12 mu in my main cash crop, cabbage, because that is where I can make money and I already know how to manage it well. Since I have well irrigation and long experience, I am willing to run three cabbage crops on that land across the year: spring, summer, and autumn. Cabbage needs more fertilizer, water, and spraying, but on my farm that is still worth it because the return is better than grain. I will use hybrid cabbage seed for stronger vigor and more uniform heads. I will till that cabbage land with rotary tillage because it is faster for me and fits intensive vegetable production.

For the other 8 mu, I will keep grain in the usual wheat-maize rotation. I will plant winter wheat first and then summer maize on the same land after wheat harvest. I will do this because grain gives me steadier output, spreads my risk, and fits local practice. Wheat and maize need less daily attention than cabbage, which matters in a two-person household. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, keep fertilizer at moderate levels, rely on my well for key irrigations, and avoid over-input where grain prices do not justify it. This way I balance cash income from cabbage with stable grain production and keep the whole farm manageable for the year.
